A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VarCon research work. Their full main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, few-shot, transfer, corruption-robustness, and representation-analysis results in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds clustering controls, training diagnostics, memory measurements, and combined-method experiments.

M1.justification: The core VarCon loss, centroid computation, and confidence-adaptive temperature procedure remain unchanged. Appendix E.2 adds VarCon+PaCo and VarCon+GPaCo hybrid variants combining the variational approach with those methods, although their integration is not specified algorithmically.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same CIFAR and ImageNet benchmarks, ImageNet-ReaL, ImageNet-C, few-shot settings, and twelve transfer datasets. The new diagnostics and hybrid comparisons use existing datasets; discussion of class imbalance and multimodality does not establish evaluation on new long-tailed or multimodal data.

E2.justification: Tables 12–13 add PaCo and GPaCo as directly relevant parametric contrastive comparators on ImageNet and CIFAR-100, materially broadening the comparison beyond v1's baseline set. Table 6 also adds fixed-temperature VarCon to the clustering comparison. The regularizers and X-CLR discussed in Tables 9–11 are conceptual comparisons, not additional experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark protocols are retained. New diagnostics specify 50-epoch ImageNet training with fixed epsilon, a 200-epoch learnable-epsilon trace, and per-device peak-memory measurement on Rank 0. Table 12 also introduces RandAugment configurations for the added comparisons; these do not establish changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands analysis through the fixed-temperature clustering control, temperature-distribution and epsilon trajectories, decomposed training-loss curves, GPU-memory profiling, and a twelve-class semantic-similarity heatmap. These examine component contributions, adaptation dynamics, computational cost, and inter-class relationships beyond v1's retained ablations and visualizations.

E5.justification: The existing mean-plus-standard-error reporting and five random few-shot subsets remain unchanged. No new seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty procedures, or significance tests are specified. Tables 7–8 describe variation of temperatures across samples, rather than uncertainty across experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores and plots are retained, but substantial new results appear. Table 6 adds fixed-temperature VarCon's ARI of 0.627; Figure 8 reports 43.09 versus 43.25 GB for VarCon and SupCon. Tables 12–13 report new hybrid results, including VarCon+GPaCo at 79.94% on ImageNet with RandAugment and 81.29% on CIFAR-100. These are additional method/configuration results, not improvements to the unchanged standalone scores.

T1.justification: Equation (3) removes v1's erroneous logarithm from the marginal-density identity. Appendix D.3 adds an O(B C_d) similarity-memory argument and the bound C_d ≤ B. The remaining ELBO development and Appendix C gradient derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: an ELBO-derived contrastive objective, confidence-adaptive supervision, stronger representations, and improved accuracy, convergence, and robustness. Headline accuracy claims remain unchanged; new supporting analyses do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.1 identifies limitations involving label dependence, centroid-computation overhead, and temperature recalibration under domain shift. Sections 4.7 and D add interpretations of adaptation and optimization dynamics, while B.4 distinguishes the loss's contribution from adaptive temperature. Appendix E.2 newly argues complementarity with class-imbalance methods.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link and documents settings for the new diagnostics, including fixed versus learnable epsilon, per-GPU batch size 512, and Rank 0 memory measurement. Existing optimizer, hardware, training-time, centroid-detachment, and epsilon-clamping information was already present. The new hybrid variants lack a detailed implementation recipe.

R1.justification: Appendices D.4 and E substantially expand positioning against adaptive regularization, multimodal contrastive learning, and class-imbalance methods. Seven references are added, including PaCo, GPaCo, AdaFocal, Dual Focal Loss, locally adaptive label smoothing, learning-from-teaching regularization, and mixup. The previously cited X-CLR receives a detailed methodological comparison.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative are retained. v3 swaps the augmentation and transfer subsections, renames the embedding-analysis paragraph, condenses the conclusion, and adds cross-references, Section 4.7, and appendix subsections. These are limited editorial and structural changes accompanying the substantive additions.

P2.justification: v3 adds temperature, loss, memory, and semantic-similarity displays in Figures 4 and 7–9, plus Tables 7–13, and expands Table 6 with an ablation row. The original t-SNE figures are retained as Figures 5–6. This substantially expands the visual presentation beyond ordinary renumbering and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The fixed-temperature control, adaptation and memory diagnostics, relevant PaCo/GPaCo comparisons, explicit limitations, and Equation (3) correction improve the paper's transparency and evidential support. The gains are limited by underspecified hybrid implementations and overinterpretation of numerical losses from different objectives as evidence of faster optimization. Broad superiority claims also remain unreconciled with the higher PaCo/GPaCo scores reported in the new comparison tables.
